text:
Maya: Heads up — we've been seeing repeated OOM spikes on prod-serving-05 over the last 2h, latency climbs and then sudden instance OOMs. :warning:
Leo: saw the alert, grabbing logs now. which model/route?
Maya: redwood-7b-8k route (chat-v2). affected tenants: a bunch of long-context sessions + some reranking bursts.
InfraBot: [automated] instance prod-serving-05 reported GPU OOMs x5 in 2h, memory reclaimed by kernel kill.
Sam: can you paste the OOM snippet? also curious about kernel selector history for that shard.
Maya: paste below:
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] ERROR cuda: out of memory (cudaMalloc)
model=redwood-7b-8k kv_cache_alloc=3.2GB workspace_request=2.1GB allocator_fragmentation=0.25
stack: serving::kv::alloc -> runtime::workspace::alloc -> cuda::alloc
```
Ria: kv_cache_alloc looks high. those long lived chat sessions accumulating prefixes. are we failing to reuse or evict?
Kevin: profiler snapshot from 13:50 shows continuous KV growth, and one call path using the slower kernel variant (kernel=matmul_slow_v2) which increases workspace.
Leo: that kernel variant was chosen by selector after a regression in kernel heuristics last week — maybe selector picked a safe-but-high-workspace path.
Sam: possible checklist:
- force kernel selector to prefer low-workspace kernels for shards with <X free memory
- enable transient KV eviction for sessions idle > 10m
- drop workspace cap for that instance to 1.2GB (temp)
- enable model-fallback to quantized variant when OOM detected
- circuit-breaker: reduce concurrency for this route
Maya: can we do an emergency mitigation now without deploy? maybe toggle runtime config: --workspace-cap=1.2GB and --kv-ttl=600?
Ria: I can flip the kv-ttl per cluster via runtime config. will do kv-ttl=600 (10m) and aggressive eviction threshold.
Kevin: I'll push a hotfix to the kernel selector flags to bias for low-workspace kernels: set KERNEL_SELECTOR_PREFERENCE=low_workspace for prod-serving-05. It is a dynamic flag.
Sam: I'll trigger the circuit-breaker rule to throttle chat-v2 to concurrency 3 for that instance and enable fallback to rw-7b-q4 for new requests.
Maya: doing traffic commands now — please monitor traces and OOM count.
InfraBot: [action] kv-ttl updated on prod-serving-05 by Ria.
Leo: rolling selector flag now. watch the kernel chosen distribution.
Kevin: kernel distribution post-flag (13:58->14:05): matmul_slow_v2 72% -> 8%, matmul_fast_low_ws 20% -> 85%, mismatched 8%
Ria: eviction logs starting at 14:03, freeing ~2.8GB of KV over 4min.
Sam: circuit-breaker engaged and fallback enabled at 14:06 — 10% of routed requests now go to rw-7b-q4 fallback.
Maya: immediate effects: memory pressure falling, OOMs stopped after 14:07. latency for fallback requests +20ms, tokens cost -35%.
Leo: good. follow-ups we should add to playbook:
- automated detection rule: if allocator free < 1.0GB and kernel_selection_bias != low_workspace, flip flag and notify oncall
- per-tenant KV TTL + max-prefix-size to avoid unbounded KV growth
- acceptance test: run long-context workload in CI with selector bias to validate no degenerate kernel picks
- telemetry: record kernel variant, workspace_requested, kv_alloc at request-level sampling
Ria: I'll own the KV TTL + eviction PR (assign to me). plan: add per-tenant max_prefix_tokens and a sliding TTL eviction to runtime.
Sam: I'll add the emergency runtime flags + docs for ops-runbook. include exact commands used today and the thresholds.
Kevin: I'll open a kernel-selector revert/patch PR to make heuristics consider worst-case workspace over recent N requests instead of instantaneous estimate.
Maya: oncall notes: if OOM surge happens again, steps in order: 1) flip selector bias, 2) lower workspace cap, 3) enable kv-ttl eviction, 4) engage circuit-breaker + fallback, 5) drain long sessions.
Leo: propose we also implement a soft-reserve buffer per instance to avoid sudden alloc chases — +200MB reserve for safety.
Ria: noted. will include reserve config in my PR.
Sam: quick QA action: roll the selector flag in canary (10%) for 30m before wider rollout. Leo can you handle?
Leo: will do. canary starting 14:20.
Maya: thanks all. filing an incident postmortem after stable. tl;dr: kernel selector regression + unbounded KV growth -> OOMs, mitigated via selector bias + TTL + fallback.
InfraBot: [automated] incident ticket created: INC-20260318-1491. assigned to eng-runtime.
Kevin: :eyes: will follow up on selector heuristics PR.
Ria: :thumbsup: I'll paste PR link here when ready.
Sam: adding runbook section now. will link to this thread in the doc.
Maya: closing loop — no new OOMs for 45m, keeping monitoring on. thanks team.
